question: How do you detect and mitigate data drift and concept drift in production inference pipelines?
model_answer: Data drift occurs when input feature distributions change ($P(X)$). Concept drift occurs when the relationship between features and targets changes ($P(Y|X)$). Detection uses statistical tests (KS-test, PSI). Mitigation involves continuous re-training triggers and fallback model routing.
key_points: Data drift P(X) vs Concept drift P(Y|X) definitions
Statistical metrics (Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, Population Stability Index PSI)
Automated pipeline re-training triggers
Shadow deployments and continuous evaluation

question: Explain INT8 quantization and structured pruning techniques for deploying LLMs onto resource-constrained edge devices.
model_answer: Quantization converts 32-bit floating point weights to 8-bit integers (INT8), reducing memory footprint by 4x. Structured pruning removes entire weight matrix rows/columns or attention heads, accelerating matrix multiplication on hardware tensor cores.
key_points: Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) vs Quantization-Aware Training (QAT)
FP32 to INT8 weight mapping and scaling factors
Structured pruning (channel/head removal) vs Unstructured pruning
Hardware tensor core acceleration and memory bandwidth reduction

question: How do you design a real-time feature store that guarantees point-in-time correctness for online prediction models?
model_answer: Feature stores (Feast) maintain dual storage: an offline store (Snowflake/Parquet) for historical point-in-time joins during training, and an online store (Redis/DynamoDB) for low-latency key-value feature retrieval during live inference.
key_points: Dual storage architecture (Offline batch store vs Online low-latency store)
Point-in-time joins (time-travel) preventing data leakage during training
Streaming ingestion (Kafka/Flink) to online feature store
Feature schema registry and version control

question: Explain the Transformer self-attention mechanism (Q, K, V) and why its computational complexity is O(N^2) with sequence length.
model_answer: Self-attention computes `Softmax(Q * K^T / sqrt(d_k)) * V`. Multiplying Query (N x d) and Key (N x d) matrices produces an N x N attention map, causing O(N^2) memory and compute scaling with sequence length N.
key_points: Query, Key, and Value vector projections
Softmax scaling factor (1/sqrt(d_k)) for gradient stability
O(N^2) quadratic complexity scaling with sequence length
Linear attention variants (FlashAttention, Sliding Window)

question: What is LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) fine-tuning? How does updating low-rank decomposition matrices drastically cut GPU memory during training?
model_answer: LoRA freezes pre-trained model weights `W` and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices `A` and `B` (`W + A*B`). Where `W` is d x d, `A` is d x r and `B` is r x d (r << d), reducing trainable parameters by 99%.
key_points: Freezing base pre-trained weight matrices W
Low-rank matrix decomposition (A * B with rank r << d)
99% reduction in trainable parameters and optimizer memory
Zero-latency merging of LoRA weights back into base model for deployment

question: Explain PagedAttention in vLLM and how dynamic KV-cache memory management eliminates GPU RAM fragmentation.
model_answer: Traditional LLM serving allocates contiguous GPU RAM for maximum sequence length KV-caches, wasting up to 60-80% RAM. PagedAttention partitions KV-caches into virtual non-contiguous memory blocks like OS virtual memory.

question: How do Population Stability Index (PSI) and Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) tests quantify feature distribution drift in production?
model_answer: PSI measures shift between baseline training data and production serving data across binned buckets (PSI > 0.2 indicates significant shift). The KS-test computes maximum distance between cumulative distribution functions.
key_points: PSI bucket frequency comparison (PSI < 0.1 stable, > 0.2 drift)
Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test non-parametric CDF distance metric
Monitoring input feature distributions vs target label distribution
Automated alerting triggers for model retraining

question: Explain gradient accumulation and distributed data parallel (DDP) training across multi-node GPU clusters.
model_answer: DDP replicates the model on each GPU, computing gradients on distinct data batches and synchronizing gradients via AllReduce. Gradient accumulation sums gradients across N micro-batches before calling `optimizer.step()`, simulating large batch sizes.
key_points: Distributed Data Parallel (DDP) model replication
AllReduce collective communication for gradient synchronization
Gradient accumulation for large effective batch sizes on limited VRAM
NCCL library GPU inter-connect optimization (NVLink)

question: What is Knowledge Distillation? How does a smaller Student model learn soft probability distributions from a large Teacher model?
model_answer: Knowledge Distillation trains a compact Student model using soft probability targets generated by a large Teacher model using a high temperature Softmax, transferring dark knowledge about inter-class relationships.
key_points: Teacher model (large, high capacity) vs Student model (compact)
Soft targets via Temperature-scaled Softmax

question: Compare Continuous Batching with static batching for multi-tenant LLM serving endpoints under variable input prompt lengths.
model_answer: Static batching waits for N requests and pads sequences to max length, wasting compute on padding tokens. Continuous batching operates at iteration level, dynamically inserting new requests as soon as completed requests finish generation.
key_points: Static batching padding overhead and head-of-line blocking

question: Explain RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding) vs Absolute Positional Encodings in modern open-weights LLMs.
model_answer: Absolute positional encodings add fixed/learned vectors to token embeddings, struggling to generalize to longer context windows. RoPE rotates Query and Key vectors in complex space based on relative position, enabling context length extrapolation.
key_points: Absolute positional encodings limitations on context length extrapolation

question: How do shadow deployments and canary deployments allow live model evaluation without impacting real candidate predictions?
model_answer: Shadow deployment clones live production traffic to a new candidate model in parallel. The candidate model processes inputs and logs predictions for offline evaluation without returning results to users, validating safety before canary rollout.

question: What is FlashAttention? How does tiling SRAM memory accesses speed up self-attention computations without HBM bandwidth bottlenecks?
model_answer: Standard attention reads/writes intermediate N x N attention matrices to High Bandwidth Memory (HBM). FlashAttention tiles Q, K, V blocks into fast GPU SRAM, computing Softmax online without materializing the full N x N matrix in HBM.
key_points: GPU memory hierarchy (SRAM speed vs HBM bandwidth bottleneck)
Tiling blocks of Q, K, V into fast SRAM
Online Softmax calculation without storing full N x N attention matrix
2x-4x speedup and O(N) memory complexity

question: Explain Speculative Decoding using a small draft model to accelerate generation from a large target model.
model_answer: Speculative decoding uses a fast, lightweight Draft model to generate K candidate tokens sequentially. The large Target model verifies all K tokens in a single parallel forward pass, accepting valid tokens and accelerating generation by 2x-3x.
key_points: Small draft model rapid token generation
Large target model single parallel verification pass
Modified rejection sampling preserving exact target model probability distribution
Latency reduction without quality degradation

question: How do SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME provide real-time feature attribution explainability for black-box models?
model_answer: SHAP calculates Shapley values from cooperative game theory, measuring each feature's marginal contribution across all feature subsets. LIME fits a local interpretable surrogate model around a specific instance prediction.
